stock.title: Oracle stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Oracle's stock forecast weighs cloud growth, infrastructure spending, cash generation, dilution and three probability-based scenarios.
stock.opening: Oracle's weighted forecast is $142.54 in October 2027. It hinges on converting cloud backlog into profitable capacity and cash returns.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Oracle's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Oracle's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast sees limited near-term upside but substantial two- and three-year potential if Oracle converts its cloud backlog into cash-generating capacity. The probability-weighted price is $142.54 in October 2027, a 2% return including dividends, rising to $216.62 in October 2028 and $312.99 in October 2029, equivalent to 56% and 126%. By October 2029, the range runs from $21.48 in the bear case to $701.39 in the bull case, against today’s $141.53.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Oracle?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes Oracle has signed demand but cannot deliver enough powered capacity profitably. Delays, weaker pricing and underused facilities keep free cash flow negative, while debt and dilution rise. The shares fall from $62.02 in October 2027 to $21.48 in October 2029. Its 30% probability reflects the $70B spending plan and the absence of proven steady-state OCI returns, though strong RPO and cloud growth make collapse less likely than not.

The bull case requires on-time capacity, broad customer demand, strong utilization, improving margins and cash flow that reduces leverage. It rises from $234.01 in October 2027 to $701.39 in October 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the number of conditions that must succeed together.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Oracle really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash reached US$31,977 million in fiscal 2026, but capital spending reached US$55,663 million. Free cash flow—operating cash less capital spending—was therefore negative US$23,686 million. Oracle reported profit, but the bank account still needed funding for OCI.

Stock compensation adds another economic cost. Fiscal 2026 stock pay was US$4,811 million; deducting it from ordinary free cash flow produces analytical “real free cash flow” of negative US$28,497 million. The cash test therefore leads directly to the balance sheet and its financing demands.

dividend.title: Oracle dividend: cash coverage and outlook
dividend.meta_description: Oracle pays $2.00 per share in the base case, while negative free cash flow makes cash coverage the key question.
dividend.opening: Oracle pays $2.00 per share in the base case through October 2027. In fiscal 2026, free cash flow was negative US$23,686 million while capital expenditure reached US$55,663 million, so the dividend was not covered by free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Oracle's business, its rivals, its management, and the risks around its growth and financing.

blocks.heading: How much does Oracle pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends remain $2.00 per share in the base case through October 2027, then rise to $2.40 by October 2029. The bear freezes them at $2.00 because FY2026 free cash flow was negative $23,686M and FY2027 net CapEx outlay is guided at $70B. The bull reaches $3.00, requiring cash conversion to improve.

blocks.heading: Is Oracle's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: In fiscal 2022, Oracle generated US$5,028 million of free cash flow but paid shareholders US$19,705 million, including US$16,248 million of buybacks. A buyback retires shares, increasing the remaining shareholders’ claim, but it cannot be funded indefinitely by current cash when payouts exceed it. Oracle also received US$26,151 million from investments sold or matured; that released previously invested money rather than creating new operating cash.

Fiscal 2023 then concentrated spending on acquisitions, with US$27,721 million of cash used, principally for Cerner. Oracle issued US$33,994 million of debt and repaid US$21,050 million. Fiscal 2024 briefly restored capacity: free cash flow reached US$11,807 million, shareholder payments were US$5,593 million, and net debt declined to US$76,208 million.

The reversal came with infrastructure spending. Free cash flow fell to negative US$394 million in fiscal 2025 and negative US$23,686 million in fiscal 2026, when capital expenditure reached US$55,663 million. A company can still be profitable in this situation. If a shop collects US$100, spends US$60 running the shop and buys a US$70 machine, it has operating cash flow of US$40 but free cash flow of negative US$30.

blocks.heading: What is Oracle's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: At **$141.53**, Oracle’s common shares are worth **$432,585.28 million**. Its trailing P/E is **22.2x**, meaning investors pay $22.20 for each dollar of earnings generated over the last twelve months. That earnings measure matters, but OCI consumes cash before the full cost of its equipment reaches the income statement.

earnings.title: Oracle earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Oracle results are expected December 14, 2026; watch whether infrastructure growth turns into cash.
earnings.opening: Oracle expects to announce its next results on December 14, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether Oracle converts commitments into accepted capacity and cash.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Oracle makes money, who it competes with, how management is paid and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: What has Oracle guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Oracle’s share-price upside depends on converting its backlog into profitable OCI capacity and durable cash returns. For the year to May 2027, management guides to at least US$90 billion of revenue and US$8.10 of non-GAAP EPS. It expects US$90–95 billion of gross capital expenditure and guides to US$70 billion of net cash outlay for CapEx.

blocks.heading: Did Oracle keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Oracle did keep one important promise. It forecast fiscal 2026 infrastructure revenue of US$18 billion in September 2025 and delivered US$18.1 billion. That growth is real, but negative free cash flow of US$23.7 billion leaves the harder question unanswered: can the new leaders turn expansion into attractive returns for the owners who fund it?

blocks.heading: What is Oracle's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: That growth still has to be delivered. A contract promises future revenue, but Oracle records cloud revenue as it provides working capacity. It must obtain GPUs, power, buildings and networking before a customer can use the service. The quarterly figures show that capacity is reaching customers: revenue rose from US$14,926 million in August 2025 to US$19,345 million in August 2026.

Diluted earnings per share, or EPS, rose from US$4.34 to US$5.83 in fiscal 2026. That increase was faster than sales, but investment gains, taxes and share-count changes also mattered. The central question is therefore whether delivered infrastructure growth can earn an attractive return after the cash needed to build it.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Oracle's next results?

paragraphs.text: Oracle expects to announce its November-quarter results on December 14, 2026, subject to change. Investors should look for accelerating infrastructure revenue, continued customer receipts and improving cash after equipment spending.
